---
title: "Job Application Optimizer"
subtitle: "Developer documentation for AI_resume_Reviewer"
---

The Job Application Optimizer takes a PDF résumé and a job description, and
uses Google Gemini to tell you how well the two match, what to change, and what
to expect from the company. It can then write a tailored résumé and cover
letter as Word documents.

These pages document how the backend works. Every code example on them is run
against the real code in this repository when the site is built, so what you read is
what the code does today.

## What it does

| Step | What happens | Where in the code |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Upload | Text is extracted from the résumé PDF | `services/pdf_service.py` |
| 2. Analyse | Gemini scores the résumé (1–10) against the job role | `services/gemini_service.py` |
| 3. ATS check | Gemini estimates an applicant-tracking-system score (0–100%) and lists missing keywords | `services/gemini_service.py` |
| 4. Research | Gemini summarises the target company | `services/gemini_service.py` |
| 5. Recommend | The analyses above are combined into interview and application advice | `services/gemini_service.py` |
| 6. Generate | A rewritten résumé and a cover letter are saved as `.docx` files | `services/document_service.py` |

## How the pieces fit

A React frontend talks to a FastAPI backend over HTTP. The backend's routers
are thin: they validate input and hand the work to three services.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  UI["React frontend<br/>(frontend/)"] -->|HTTP| API["FastAPI routers<br/>(api/)"]
  API --> PDF["pdf_service<br/>PyPDF2"]
  API --> GEM["gemini_service<br/>Google Gemini"]
  API --> DOC["document_service<br/>python-docx"]
  GEM -->|prompts| CLOUD[("Gemini API")]
  DOC --> OUT[/"outputs/*.docx"/]
```

## The API at a glance

This table is generated from the application itself: it imports the FastAPI
app and lists its registered routes, with the first line of each endpoint's
docstring. If a route is added, renamed or removed, the table changes with it.

```{python}
#| echo: false
import os, sys, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(".."))

# app.py creates uploads/ and outputs/ in the working directory on import,
# so import it from a throwaway folder to keep the docs project clean.
here = os.getcwd()
os.chdir(tempfile.mkdtemp())
try:
    import app as backend
finally:
    os.chdir(here)

from fastapi.routing import APIRoute
from IPython.display import Markdown

api_routes = [
    r for r in backend.app.routes
    if isinstance(r, APIRoute) and r.path.startswith("/api/")
]

rows = ["| Method | Path | Area | Purpose |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
for r in api_routes:
    method = ", ".join(sorted(r.methods))
    purpose = (r.endpoint.__doc__ or "").strip().splitlines()[0]
    rows.append(f"| `{method}` | `{r.path}` | {', '.join(r.tags)} | {purpose} |")

Markdown("\n".join(rows))
```

The app exposes `{python} len(api_routes)` API endpoints. It also serves
`/health`, `/info`, interactive API docs at `/docs`, and the built React
frontend from `/`.

## Running it locally

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Dharundp6/AI_resume_Reviewer-.git
cd AI_resume_Reviewer-
pip install -r requirements.txt
cd frontend && npm install && cd ..
echo GEMINI_API_KEY=your_key_here > .env
python app.py          # backend on http://localhost:8000
```

The frontend runs separately with `npm start` inside `frontend/`, on
<http://localhost:3000>. Every step except the upload needs a Gemini API key.
That includes document generation: Gemini writes the résumé and cover letter,
and python-docx only formats them.
